due_when.clears_when: The next e35 sweep writes a history sidecar in which every archived row's `superseded_by_sweep` names a DIFFERENT run than its own `sweep_generated_at`, and the archived count equals the number of keys genuinely displaced. Proposed remedy, one line and structural: rename the aggregate artifact so the corpus job's glob cannot match it (`e35-bracket-ALL` -> a name outside `e35-bracket-*`), which stops the duplicate being produced rather than de-duplicating it afterwards. A dedup inside `e35_corpus_extract.py` keyed on `measurement_key` would also work and is more robust to a future artifact name, but it hides the double-download rather than removing it. NOT closed by reasoning about the workflow: it needs an actual sweep whose sidecar is read back.

what: [research] The e35 sweep's `corpus` job scans every leg's report.json TWICE, so the history sidecar shipped by #10583 archives 51% same-run duplicates instead of superseded measurements. Measured on run 33411906178, the sidecar's FIRST live exercise: 10,547 archived rows, of which 5,174 are genuine supersedes (per-leg source path, keys still live in the corpus carrying the new measurement) and 5,373 are copies of THAT RUN'S OWN rows (source path under `collected/e35-bracket-ALL/`). 5,373 is exactly 27 legs x ~199 cells -- every row the run produced, written twice and archived once.
